summary.text: Big Thief's Northeast tour targets five cities near Qloo fan hotspots, where audiences share taste for introspective folk-indie and straightforward melodic songwriting. Rooms of 300–900 (our own target) in intimate venues across Boston, Burlington, Portland ME, Northampton and Albany align with the audience's affinity for vulnerability and human-centred narrative.

theme.text: Vulnerability & Introspection: Posters and stage design centre on intimate close-ups, handwritten lyrics, and minimal staging that foregrounds the emotional core of each song.
Northeast Folk Lineage: Visual campaign connects Big Thief to the folk and indie songwriting tradition of New England, using archival imagery and regional references.
Human Experience: Thematic storytelling in social media and merch focuses on grief, confession and sensitivity—resonating with audience taste for authentic narrative.

merch.text: Lyric prints: Framed single lyrics from the setlist in minimalist typography, reflecting the straightforward confessional style fans favour.
Collaborations with heritage outdoor brands (Patagonia, Fjällräven, REI-adjacent): Embroidered Big Thief patches or limited-run tote bags appeal to audience affinity for quality, conscious materials.
Handwritten journals: Small notebooks with Big Thief quotes and blank pages, inviting fans' own confessional writing—reinforcing the vulnerability and introspection core to the brand.

risks.text: Room affinity measures taste overlap, not confirmed demand or ticket sales. Booking all five cities simultaneously requires coordination across venues and dates.
All five stops cluster geographically; routing and neighbouring dates with other acts may affect availability or fan travel. Validate interest with each venue before committing.

Ages 24-and-younger and 30–34 show positive affinity; ages 45+ show significant negative index. Tour messaging and promotion should reflect actual audience composition, not the full demographic spectrum.
